You need to build a full Blazor Server team messaging chat page in the project at `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b`. The project uses .NET 11, Blazor Server with interactive server render mode, and Bootstrap CSS is available. The root namespace is `sv_9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b`. ## What to create ### 1. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Services/ChatModels.cs` Contains the record types and interface: ```csharp namespace sv_9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b.Services; public record Channel(int Id, string Name, string Description, int UnreadCount); public record Message(int Id, int ChannelId, string Author, string Content, DateTime SentAt, int? ReplyToId, List Reactions); public record Reaction(string Emoji, List Users); public record ThreadSummary(int RootMessageId, int ReplyCount, DateTime LastReplyAt); public interface IChatService { Task> GetChannelsAsync(); Task> GetMessagesAsync(int channelId, int skip, int take); Task SendMessageAsync(int channelId, string content, int? replyToId); Task> GetThreadAsync(int rootMessageId); Task AddReactionAsync(int messageId, string emoji); Task MarkChannelReadAsync(int channelId); } ``` ### 2. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Services/MockChatService.cs` A mock implementation of `IChatService` that returns realistic sample data so the page works out of the box. Include: - 4-5 channels (general, random, engineering, design, announcements) - ~15-20 messages spread across channels with realistic content, authors, timestamps (use DateTime.UtcNow minus various TimeSpans), some with reactions - Some messages should be thread starters (have replies linked via ReplyToId) - GetThreadAsync should return the root message + replies - SendMessageAsync should create a new message and return it - AddReactionAsync should add the emoji to the message (or add current user "You" to existing reaction) - MarkChannelReadAsync should set unread count to 0 - GetMessagesAsync should respect skip/take for pagination - Store data in memory (lists/dictionaries) ### 3. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Components/Pages/Chat.razor` The main chat page with route `/chat` and `@rendermode InteractiveServer`. This is a complex component with three panels: **Layout structure:** A flex container with three panels side by side, full viewport height (use `100vh`). The chat page should NOT use the default MainLayout — use `@layout` with a minimal layout or `@attribute [Layout(typeof(ChatLayout))]` — actually simplest is to just use the default layout but override styles. Better: create a dedicated `ChatLayout.razor` that just renders `@Body` with no chrome. **Left sidebar (~250px fixed width, dark background like #1a1a2e or #2b2d42):** - Header: app name "TeamChat" styled - List of channels, each clickable - Each channel item shows: `# channel-name`, truncated description, and if unread > 0 a badge - Active channel gets a highlight background - Style: dark sidebar with light text, hover effects **Main message area (flex-grow, takes remaining space):** - Header bar: shows `# channel-name` and description, with a subtle bottom border - Scrollable message list (flex-grow, overflow-y auto). Give it an id like `message-list` for JS scroll interop. - Each message is a card-like row with: - Author avatar placeholder (colored circle with initial) - Author name (bold) + relative timestamp ("just now", "2 min ago", "1 hour ago", "Yesterday", or date) - Message content text - Reaction badges row: each reaction shows emoji + count in a small pill/badge, clickable to toggle your reaction - On hover: show action buttons (Reply, React) — use CSS `:hover` on the message container to show/hide an action bar - If the message has thread replies (check via a ThreadSummaries dictionary), show "N replies" link that opens the thread panel - React button: on click, show a small popup/dropdown with 5-6 common emojis (👍 ❤️ 😂 🎉 👀 🔥) that calls AddReactionAsync - Message input at bottom: a textarea + Send button. Send on button click or Ctrl+Enter. After sending, clear the input and the new message appears. - Infinite scroll up: detect scroll to top (via JS interop) to load older messages (increment skip by take amount). Show a loading indicator when fetching. **Right thread panel (~350px fixed width, shown conditionally):** - Only visible when a thread is open (user clicked "Reply" or "N replies") - Header: "Thread" title + close (X) button - Shows the original/root message quoted at top (styled differently, like a quote block) - Scrollable list of reply messages below - Reply input at bottom: textarea + "Reply" button. Sends via SendMessageAsync with replyToId set. - When closed, the main area expands to fill the space. **State management in the component:** - `List channels` - `Channel? activeChannel` - `List messages` (for current channel) - `Dictionary threadSummaries` — built from messages (group by ReplyToId, count replies) - `int? openThreadRootId` — which thread is open - `List? threadMessages` — messages in the open thread - `string newMessage` — bound to main input - `string newReply` — bound to thread input - `int skip = 0; int take = 25;` - `bool loadingMore` - `int? emojiPickerMessageId` — which message has the emoji picker open - `bool isLoading` — initial loading state **Key methods:** - `OnInitializedAsync`: load channels, select first, load its messages - `SelectChannel(Channel)`: set active, reset skip, load messages, mark read, close thread - `LoadMessages()`: call GetMessagesAsync, build thread summaries - `LoadOlderMessages()`: increment skip, prepend older messages - `SendMessage()`: call SendMessageAsync, append to list, clear input - `OpenThread(int rootMessageId)`: set openThreadRootId, load thread via GetThreadAsync - `CloseThread()`: clear thread state - `SendReply()`: call SendMessageAsync with replyToId, append to thread messages, update thread summary - `ToggleReaction(int messageId, string emoji)`: call AddReactionAsync, update local state - `ShowEmojiPicker(int messageId)` / hide - `FormatRelativeTime(DateTime)`: helper for relative timestamps - `GetAvatarColor(string author)`: deterministic color from author name hash ### 4. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Components/Pages/Chat.razor.css` Scoped CSS for the chat page. Use CSS isolation. Include all styles for: - The three-panel flex layout - Sidebar styles (dark theme, channel list, active state, unread badge) - Message area styles (header, scrollable list, message cards, hover actions, reactions) - Thread panel styles (slide-in feel, quote block, reply list) - Emoji picker popup styles - Message input area styles - Loading indicators - Responsive considerations (min-widths) - Smooth transitions for thread panel open/close ### 5. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Components/Pages/Chat.razor.js` A collocated JS module for scroll interop: - `scrollToBottom(element)`: scrolls a container to the bottom - `onScrollToTop(element, dotNetRef)`: sets up an IntersectionObserver or scroll listener to detect when user scrolls to the top, then invokes a .NET method `[JSInvokable] LoadOlderMessages` - `dispose()`: cleanup listeners ### 6. `/tmp/sv-9b4bba9dac6b4d8495f4f1c0cb879a4b/Components/Layout/ChatLayout.razor` A minimal layout just for the chat page: ```razor @inherits LayoutComponentBase
